features.headline: Why Bengals' 2025 first-rounder Stewart can't crack lineup
features.desc: Stewart hasn't seen action in three games this season despite being healthy enough to play.
body: CINCINNATI — Nothing about Shemar Stewart's NFL career has been very straightforward.

From the moment the Cincinnati Bengals drafted the former Texas A&M defensive end in the first round, Stewart's path to the field has been riddled with various roadblocks. And as he approaches the end of his second NFL season, it's not easy to figure out what bulldozer is needed to clear his way.
Monday's loss to the Washington Commanders marked the third time in 2026 that Stewart didn't see any game action despite being healthy enough to play. He logged zero snaps in the 22-20 loss.
With seven games left in the regular season, the only thing Stewart and the Bengals coaching staff can do is explore every possible avenue available to get the once-prized asset into the rotation.

"We're going to need him," Bengals defensive coordinator Al Golden said on Wednesday. "This is a long stretch we have in front of us and whatever I have to do to help him and to get him into the game and impact the game, I am committed to doing that."
The need couldn't have appeared any greater at Washington. Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy, Cincinnati's starting edge rushers, respectively logged 93% and 88% of the team's defensive snaps.

Bengals coach Zac Taylor noted Mafe and Murphy felt good as the game dragged on, in part because of the extended time between some of the defensive series. But still, he acknowledged the need for more rotation.
Outside of those players, Cedric Johnson was the only true defensive end to play against Washington. Johnson played 19% of the team's 68 defensive snaps.

features.headline: Wemby tops Luka in MVP duel, Spurs teach Lakers valuable playoff lesson
features.desc: Victor Wembanyama's Spurs got the better of Luka Doncic's Lakers in an NBA Cup game with playoff-like intensity on Friday night.
body: The NBA's two main characters met for the first time this season Friday in a fierce contest that was still in doubt until the final buzzer sounded.

Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs got the better of Luka Doncic's Los Angeles Lakers, but only after erasing a 20-point deficit to grind out a 99-96 victory at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio.

Round 1 between the two MVP favorites doubled as a do-or-die NBA Cup contest. By winning, the Spurs advanced to the in-season tournament's quarterfinals, eliminated the Lakers and reclaimed the Western Conference's No. 1 seed in one fell swoop.

While Wembanyama and Doncic served as compelling foils, this highly anticipated showdown between European superstars was ultimately decided by their respective supporting casts. San Antonio prevailed in a game with playoff-like intensity because Wembanyama enjoyed just a little more help.
"I liked how my guys reacted," Wembanyama said. "It just showed character."
Wembanyama, enormous in size and stoic in demeanor, finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, two blocks and four steals.

The 7-foot-4 French center delivered his strongest MVP argument midway through the fourth quarter, driving past center Walker Kessler for a two-hand reverse dunk on one end before swatting guard Collin Sexton's shot on the Lakers' next possession.
It's hard to imagine a player more valuable than Wembanyama because — like the movie — he has a knack for being "Everything Everywhere All at Once."
But then there's the fiery Doncic, who scored 13 of his game-high 31 points during one of his signature tone-setting first-quarter bursts.

features.headline: The Connor McDavid Scoring Tracker: Can the Oilers' superstar break 200 points?
features.desc: Follow along game by game as No. 97 looks to break a benchmark that only No. 99 has done in NHL history.
body: There have been only four occasions in NHL history when a player scored 200 or more points in a single season, and only one player has accomplished the feat: Wayne Gretzky.
The Great One scored 215 points in 1985-86, 212 in '81-82, 208 in '84-85 and 205 in '83-84. Mario Lemieux came closest to Gretzky, finishing the '88-89 season with 199.
Connor McDavid plays for the same Edmonton Oilers franchise that Gretzky did when he posted those totals, and his personal best total is 153, set in 2022-23.
There are cases for and against McDavid breaking the 200-point barrier this season, as his pace fluctuates on a game-by-game basis.
Follow along below to monitor his pace after every game, along with highlights of memorable moments along the way.
Note that this page will be updated after each game, so come back to keep tabs on McDavid as the season continues.

features.headline: Five unsung heroes of the Bears' 6-game win streak
features.desc: The Bears' stars get the headlines, but these five players have been just as important for the NFC North leaders.
body: CHICAGO — With sole possession of first place in the NFC North on the line in arguably the most consequential Thanksgiving game in franchise history, the Chicago Bears walked into Detroit's Ford Field trying to survive the short-turnaround chess match and keep Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs from strengthening his Offensive Player of the Year candidacy.

That part of the game plan didn't work as Gibbs broke loose for 205 yards on 21 carries and three rushing touchdowns, including a 70-yard burst on which he reached 21.72 mph, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That was his fastest speed as a ball carrier this season.
That touchdown put the Bears in an 11-point deficit with 8:20 left in the fourth quarter.

With 2:22 to play and the Lions threatening again from just outside Chicago's red zone, linebacker T.J. Edwards knew he couldn't be tepid in the way he went after Gibbs once the Lions decided to go for it on fourth down.
"I knew it was going to come down to that and I wanted to take a shot," Edwards said. "I knew I couldn't sit there and let him move around and had to go get him."

The look that the Lions presented on fourth-and-4 at the Bears' 33-yard line was one that Edwards recognized and acted on quickly. It led to an open-field tackle and the captain dropping Gibbs short of the sticks.

"We know all about Gibbs' speed — his ability to make guys miss in space like that," coach Ben Johnson said. "For T.J. to be able to use his instincts and take a great angle like that and make sure he got him down — that was a five-star play."

features.headline: How has Fernando Mendoza played in his first two starts?
features.desc: We took a look at what Raiders' Fernando Mendoza did well — and not so well — in his first two starts.
body: HENDERSON, Nev. — Fernando Mendoza's 11th pass attempt against the Denver Broncos on Sunday showed coach Klint Kubiak what the Las Vegas Raiders' starting quarterback was made of.

The Raiders faced a third-and-long from their 13-yard line after Mendoza was sacked for a 10-yard loss. But the No. 1 pick didn't falter. As Denver rushed four defenders, Mendoza fired a 19-yard pass to second-year wide receiver Jack Bech, who made a leaping two-handed grab to keep the drive alive.
Two plays later, Mendoza found the end zone. He threw a 68-yard touchdown pass to Ashton Jeanty on a wheel route, and the Raiders' comeback hopes were alive.
"That's who he is," Kubiak said. "I think back to us being backed up, taking a sack, and then him making a really big third-and-long throw to Jack Bech. That's what you need from your quarterback."
Mendoza's transition from backup to starter hasn't been easy. The Raiders have lost two straight, and Mendoza has dealt with a fair share of hits and rookie mistakes.

Through it all, Mendoza has displayed traits that have the organization hopeful he will flourish as the franchise's quarterback. The next step for Mendoza will be to secure his first win as a starter.
He looks to do so against the Cleveland Browns on "Sunday Night Football" (Nov. 29, 8:20 p.m. ET) — his first career primetime game and one with playoff implications.
History suggests Mendoza will have a chance to win, as rookie quarterbacks have a combined 9-6 record and a 13-10 touchdown-interception ratio in their first primetime game.

features.headline: A must-listen: KC Concepcion's powerful message on stuttering
features.desc: There's more to the story for this Browns rookie receiver: "Me being able to inspire people all over the world, it just means everything."
body: KC CONCEPCION DREADED one of the more customary parts of the NFL scouting combine.

Amid the weeklong hustle and bustle of workouts, medical testing and team interviews, 2026 draft prospects participated in news conferences with the hundreds of media members gathered for the event in Indianapolis in February.

The 5-foot-11, 196-pound wide receiver was hesitant to talk, but he obliged. He walked to the dais in front of dozens of assembled reporters and fielded questions for several minutes. He occasionally stumbled over his words, pausing and repeating himself before he finished his thoughts.
But Concepcion pushed through, and his interview went viral.
Millions watched online, most learning for the first time that Concepcion had a stutter.

Social media was littered with comments, many poking fun at the first-team All-American's speech impediment. However, just as many applauded Concepcion for having the courage to still go through with the once-dreaded interview.
According to the Cleveland Clinic, stuttering affects between 1% and 2.4% of children and 0.3% to 1% of adults, with the speech disorder affecting the rhythm and flow of how one talks.
Early on, Concepcion and his parents noticed his speech was impacted, but as he grew older, he worked to make sure it wouldn't define him.
And now, as a top contender for the NFL's Offensive Rookie of the Year award, what was once a source of bullying and insecurity has transformed into a lifelong passion for advocacy.

When the Browns host the Las Vegas Raiders on "Sunday Night Football" (8:20 ET, NBC), Concepcion will once again bring awareness to speech impediments with his custom-made cleats as part of the NFL's My Cause My Cleats initiative.
